title: Test-scope detection misses Rust tests/*.rs and all Dart test code
description:
sutra/290 excluded `#[cfg(test)]` code from constraint evaluation via `LanguageAdapter::test_line_ranges`, which is attribute-driven. Two gaps remain:

1. **Rust integration tests.** Files under a crate's `tests/` (and `benches/`) directory are test targets in their entirety but carry no `cfg(test)` attribute, so every match in them still reports. The current mitigation is scoping rules to `src/` — which the vidhi catalog does, so this is latent rather than actively painful.

2. **Dart.** `DartAdapter` uses the default empty `test_line_ranges`. Dart's conventions are path-based (`test/` directory) plus `@visibleForTesting`, so the fix shape differs from Rust's.

Both want a path-based classifier alongside the range-based one. The design question that stopped sutra/290 from just doing it: a rule deliberately scoped to `tests/` would go silently inert under a blanket path exclusion. Options considered but not decided — (a) skip path exclusion when the constraint's own scope resolves into a test path, (b) require `include_tests` and surface a dead_constraint finding when a test-scoped rule matches nothing, (c) leave path exclusion opt-in via a workspace-level setting.

Not urgent: the `src/`-scoping mitigation is what every adopted catalog already does.

decisions.decision: Test-path exclusion steps aside when a constraint's own scope literal-prefixes into a test path (option a), rather than requiring include_tests plus a dead_constraint finding (b) or a workspace-level opt-in setting (c).
decisions.rationale: Needs no new user-facing concept and no new config surface: a rule written for `tests/**` obviously means tests, and that intent is readable from data already on the constraint. Only the literal prefix counts, so `**/*.rs` and unscoped rules still get the default exclusion.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: (b) require include_tests + emit a dead_constraint finding — makes the common case (a rule genuinely aimed at tests) fail first and teach second, and adds a finding kind to the coverage machinery for one narrow case. (c) workspace-level opt-in setting — leaves the false-positive flood on by default for every unconfigured adopter, which is the failure sutra/290 was filed for.

execution_record:
Landed as designed; no failed approaches. Two things worth knowing for the next editor:

- The Dart `test/` prefix check already existed in `dart::extract_flags` (symbol FLAG_CFG_TEST) but was narrower — `starts_with("test/")` only, missing monorepo paths like `packages/ui/test/`. Extracting `dart::is_test_path` widened symbol flagging as a side effect; intended, but it is a behavioral change beyond constraints.
- Checked the contract boundary explicitly: `Graph::import_edges()` (pagerank, impact, blast radius) is unfiltered and stays that way; only `production_import_edges()` honours is_test. Flagging test-target imports therefore does not move any ranking or impact number.

Python/C/JS-TS were left at the default `is_test_path == false`, even though python.rs and c.rs already have `is_test_file` helpers feeding symbol flags. Wiring those into constraint evaluation is a real follow-up (their test files still report), deliberately out of scope here — filed as sutra/295.

Measurement (sutra's own tests/, unscoped no-unwrap rule): 2989 matches before, 0 after, all 2989 still reachable with include_tests = true. Full suite 1501 passed; clippy warning count identical to baseline (677).

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review of c483406..77b48f8 (sutra/292 293 294 295). Verdict: needs-attention.

[high] Test-scoped dep and cycle rules are still dropped by production-edge filtering (src/constraints/check.rs:336, 435)
The `scope_targets_tests` escape hatch introduced by this task exists ONLY in patterns.rs (confirmed: `rg scope_targets_tests` returns 5 hits, all in src/constraints/patterns.rs). The DD dep path filters on `!c.include_tests && !production_edges.contains(...)` and the cycle path on `matched.is_some_and(|c| c.include_tests)` — neither consults the constraint's own scope. Since `is_test_path` now marks every import under `tests/` as is_test, a `forbidden_dep from = "tests/**"` or a `no_cycles` scoped to `tests/**` matches the raw DD graph and is then discarded unless the author also sets `include_tests = true`. That is the escape-hatch contract holding for one constraint kind and silently not for the others — and it fails in the dangerous direction (a deliberately test-targeted blocking rule goes inert with no signal).
Recommendation: apply the same literal test-target detection before dropping test-only edges in the dep and cycle paths; regression tests for `forbidden_dep from = "tests/**"` and `no_cycles scope = "tests/**"` without include_tests.

[medium] External include_tests can be shadowed by an earlier default rule (src/constraints/external.rs:228-235)
`check_import_items` takes the FIRST match from `match_external`, then applies test filtering. A broad rule appearing before a narrower `include_tests = true` rule wins the match, the test item is skipped, and the opt-in rule never evaluates. Same first-match behaviour blocks a test-path-specific external rule (`from = "tests/**"`) from firing by default. Rule-order-dependent false negative in a blocking path. Note first-match semantics predate this change; the new filter inherits the property.
Recommendation: iterate all matching external constraints, apply test filtering per constraint (including the test-directed escape hatch), and dedupe by `(constraint_id, from_path, crate)` rather than `(from_path, crate)`.

[low, documented tradeoff] Guard edge enforcement ignores include_tests (src/guard.rs:552-579)
Codex flagged this as medium; downgrading — the code carries an explicit comment stating the guard drops is_test imports unconditionally by design, because the review path still enforces and an edit-time deny on test wiring is the sutra/290 failure mode. Raising only so the tradeoff is a conscious one: with `include_tests = true` explicitly set, the guard still will not enforce.

Clean: Codex found no defect in the structural cfg predicate parser (sutra/293), the 0054/0055/0056 content_hash-clearing migrations, the singleton-SCC production self-loop fix, or the per-language is_test_path overrides (sutra/295).
